deviations.what: A third guard was added beyond the one asked for: that .github/workflows contains exactly one workflow file.
deviations.why: The constraint said the scheduled run must be the same workflow and not a second copy, because two copies of a check drift. Nothing enforced that, so the constraint would have survived exactly as long as the next person remembered it.
deviations.impact: Adding a second workflow file now fails the suite, which is a real constraint on future changes and is stated here so it is a decision rather than a surprise.

questions_for_advisor: The command's own question — should the scheduled run also assert the README's advertised promise? — is the owner's, and I have not acted on it. My recommendation, for whatever it is worth to the ruling: NO. That promise is only observable on a live run, which costs money, and a daily paid job is a standing spend nobody authorised. B18's guards already assert the promise's mechanism for free, and ARCH-20260922-010 tests it live under a pre-registration.

§30 ends with a general form that may deserve a convention: a check that runs only when something changes measures CHANGES, never STATE. Every event-triggered instrument in this repo has that shape. The question to ask of each is whether anyone would find out if the thing it watches went wrong and then nothing happened. I have not written it as a convention because generalising from one incident is the error convention 23 guards against, and one is one.
